title: Bike Lanes, Car Traffic, and Crashes
headline: Where bike lanes went in, car traffic fell — but crashes per car did not.
description: Bike lane mileage tracked against car traffic and crash rates across 18 cities. Traffic fell where lanes went in; crashes per car did not.
data_notice: The numbers on this page are invented. They were generated by a script for a training exercise and describe no real city.
chart_title: Car traffic decline after new bike lanes, by city (%)
source_name: Synthetic sample data generated for this repository
method_note: These figures are made up. They were generated by a script, not measured, and no city in this table was studied — do not cite them. What is real is the shape of the comparison: car traffic is measured before and after lane construction, and crashes are shown as a rate per 10,000 daily car trips rather than as a raw count, because fewer cars on the road means fewer crashes even when nothing has actually gotten safer. A before-and-after comparison like this one cannot separate the effect of bike lanes from anything else that changed over the same period. Replace data/source.csv with real data to make this page mean something.
author: WW Chin
